comments.content: - **[Blocking] `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.cpp:1502`** — The three definitions take only `std::string` and access instance members, but the declarations added in `DrawViewPart.h` are `static` and take `(App::DocumentObject*, std::string)`. Building `TechDraw` → compilation fails with “no declaration matches” for all three methods.

- **[Blocking] `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawUtil.h:251`** — Removing these members leaves existing calls in `CosmeticExtension.cpp` to `DU::isCosmeticVertex`, `DU::isCosmeticEdge`, and `DU::isCenterLine`. Compiling that translation unit → errors that these functions are not members of `DrawUtil`.

**1. Deleted functions still called — build break.**
The diff removes `DrawUtil::isCosmeticVertex` / `isCosmeticEdge` / `isCenterLine` (DrawUtil.cpp hunk at line 1852, DrawUtil.h hunk at line 249), but `CosmeticExtension.cpp` still calls all three at lines 71, 77–78 (`DU` is `DrawUtil` via `using DU = DrawUtil;` at line 37):
- `CosmeticExtension.cpp:71` → `DU::isCosmeticVertex(getOwner(), name)` — no such member anymore, compile error
- `CosmeticExtension.cpp:77-78` → `DU::isCosmeticEdge(getOwner(), name)` / `DU::isCenterLine(getOwner(), name)` — same

I grepped the entire repo: these are the only remaining callers of the removed API, and the diff touches only 4 files, none of which is CosmeticExtension.cpp (`src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawUtil.*` now contain zero matches for these names). Failure scenario: any build of the TechDraw App module → `'isCosmeticVertex' is not a member of 'TechDraw::DrawUtil'` (and two more), build fails.

**2. Declaration/definition signature mismatch — build break.**
`DrawViewPart.h:242-244` declares:
```cpp
static bool isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
static bool isCosmeticEdge(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
static bool isCenterLine(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
```
but `DrawViewPart.cpp:1502, 1513, 1523` define them as non-static single-argument members (`bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string element)` etc.). A member function definition with a signature not declared in the class is ill-formed — C++ requires the declaration to match, so the compiler rejects `no declaration matches 'bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string)'`. Even if it compiled, the definitions never use the `owner` parameter the declared API (and the surviving CosmeticExtension.cpp callers, which pass `getOwner()` as first argument) require — the two halves of the move simply don't connect, so `deleteCosmeticElements()` would have no working predicate in any repaired version.
